subject: biochemistry
title: Reactive oxygen species: generation, antioxidant defenses, and reperfusion injury

steps.tx: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are inevitable byproducts of aerobic metabolism. In mitochondria, electron leakage at Complexes I and III transfers single electrons to molecular oxygen, generating **superoxide** radical (O2-). Superoxide is dismutated by superoxide dismutase (SOD) into hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). In the presence of free ferrous iron (Fe2+), hydrogen peroxide undergoes the **Fenton** reaction to generate the hydroxyl radical (OH.), the most reactive and damaging biological free radical known.
steps.say: Mitochondrial electron leakage generates superoxide radicals, which superoxide dismutase converts to hydrogen peroxide. Free ferrous iron drives the Fenton reaction, generating highly toxic hydroxyl radicals that attack lipids, proteins, and DNA.

steps.tx: Cellular **antioxidant** defenses neutralize reactive oxygen species through tiered enzymatic systems. Superoxide dismutase converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide. Peroxisomal **catalase** decomposes hydrogen peroxide directly into water and oxygen. Glutathione peroxidase utilizes reduced glutathione (GSH) to reduce hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides to water and lipid alcohols, generating oxidized glutathione (GSSG). Glutathione reductase then regenerates GSH using NADPH supplied by the pentose phosphate pathway.
steps.say: Antioxidant enzymes protect cells from oxidative stress. Superoxide dismutase creates hydrogen peroxide, catalase converts it to water, and glutathione peroxidase reduces peroxides using reduced glutathione, which glutathione reductase regenerates via NADPH.

steps.tx: Phagocytic cells intentionally generate massive ROS to kill engulfed pathogens via the **respiratory burst**. Membrane-bound **NADPH oxidase** transfers electrons from NADPH to oxygen, producing superoxide within the phagosome. Superoxide dismutates to hydrogen peroxide, which neutrophil myeloperoxidase combines with chloride to generate hypochlorous acid (bleach). In Chronic Granulomatous Disease, X-linked deficiency of NADPH oxidase prevents ROS generation, leading to recurrent catalase-positive bacterial and fungal infections.
steps.say: Neutrophils generate respiratory bursts via NADPH oxidase to produce superoxide and hypochlorous acid via myeloperoxidase. Defects in NADPH oxidase cause Chronic Granulomatous Disease, causing recurrent infections from catalase-positive organisms like Staphylococcus.

steps.tx: Ischemia-reperfusion injury exemplifies destructive oxidative pathology. During tissue ischemia, cellular ATP degrades to hypoxanthine while xanthine dehydrogenase converts to **xanthine oxidase**. Upon restoration of oxygenated blood flow, xanthine oxidase metabolizes accumulated hypoxanthine, producing a massive burst of superoxide and hydrogen peroxide. Unchecked free radicals peroxidize membrane polyunsaturated fatty acids, forming malondialdehyde and triggering myocardial stunning or endothelial microvascular plugging.
steps.say: Reperfusion injury occurs when re-oxygenation allows xanthine oxidase to oxidize accumulated hypoxanthine, unleasing a burst of superoxide. Free radicals induce lipid peroxidation, damaging cell membranes and worsening ischemic injury.
